dependencies.purpose: read the rendered file back and compare it with what was requested (ffmpeg_skill.status)

execution.argv_recorder: render and preview run HyperFrames with a Node preload (node --require lib/argv-recorder.cjs) that records the argv of every chrome, ffmpeg and ffprobe process it starts, then starts it unchanged; no shell, no generated script (docs/design-decisions.md D10)

requirements.chromium: headless-capable Chrome/Chromium or chrome-headless-shell: bundled or system, detected

not_provided: free-form animation (only fade / slide / zoom layer transitions)

tools.description: Render one video per row of a CSV or JSON file through a template (e.g. every speaker's lower third from the programme sheet). Every row is validated before the first render; each output is verified like render's.
tools.dry_run: reads and validates every row against the template and reports each planned output, its expected frame count and name; launches neither Chrome nor ffmpeg and writes nothing

codec.description: h264 (.mp4), vp9 (.webm) or prores (.mov, keeps alpha)

dryRun.description: validate and plan without launching Chrome or ffmpeg or writing files

encoding.description: text encoding of a CSV file

failFast.description: stop at the first row that fails (the rest are reported as skipped)

font.description: font file shipped with every row's scene and used first for all text (see template --font)

json.description: print one JSON result document on stdout

nameField.description: column whose value names each file (<row number>-<value>); default: the row number only

overwrite.description: replace this batch's own outputs and scene directories if they exist

template.description: template every row fills (see `template --list`); the columns are its value names

workers.description: parallel capture workers per render: auto or 1-8

inputs: a .csv (header row = template value names) or .json (array of objects) file
tools.name: batch
tools.output_schema: {status, output (dir), template, rows: [{index, name, output, status: completed|failed|skipped, verified, expected, error?}], summary: {total, completed, failed, skipped}, verified, verification[] (one step per row), commands}
outputs: one video per row in the output directory
the scene directory of each row under <output>/scenes/

tools.description: Probe this machine now: Node version, the pinned hyperframes package, ffmpeg/ffprobe and their encoders, a working headless Chromium, free temp space, and whether an ffmpeg-skill checkout is present for render's cross-check (optional). Each capability is available, missing or unknown; nothing is reported that was not probed.
tools.dry_run: lists the probes it would run (argv) and runs none of them

chromiumProbe.description: skip launching Chromium (chromium:headless is then unknown, never available)

dryRun.description: validate and plan without launching Chrome or ffmpeg or writing files

json.description: print one JSON result document on stdout

tools.name: doctor
tools.output_schema: {status, ok, exit_code, capabilities: {<name>: {status: available|missing|unknown, detail, ...}}, tools: {<tool>: {usable: yes|no|unknown, missing?, unknown?}}, fonts: {scripts: {ja|zh-cn|ko: {status, family, file, fonts_covering, detail}}, advice} (informational, never affects ok), requirements, commands}

tools.description: Fast proxy render of a scene directory for checking layout and timing before the full render: lower frame rate, HyperFrames' draft encoder preset, optionally only the first N seconds. Same resolution as the scene.
tools.dry_run: same as render: validates and reports the planned command and expected frame count; launches neither Chrome nor ffmpeg and writes nothing

dryRun.description: validate and plan without launching Chrome or ffmpeg or writing files

json.description: print one JSON result document on stdout

maxDuration.description: render only the first N seconds (a staged copy of the scene is shortened; the scene itself is untouched)

timeout.description: kill the render after this long; 0 disables

tools.name: preview
tools.output_schema: same as render, plus truncated (true when --max-duration cut the scene short)

tools.description: Read a media file back with ffprobe: duration, resolution, fps, frame count, codecs.
tools.dry_run: read-only: ffprobe still runs under --dry-run (measuring is the tool's whole job); nothing is written either way

countFrames.description: do not decode to count frames when the container does not state them (frames is then null)

dryRun.description: validate and plan without launching Chrome or ffmpeg or writing files

json.description: print one JSON result document on stdout

tools.name: probe
tools.output_schema: {status, probe: {file, format, duration, size_bytes, bitrate, video: {codec, profile, width, height, fps, r_frame_rate, frames, frames_source, pix_fmt} | null, audio: {codec, channels, sample_rate} | null}, commands}
outputs: a JSON description of the file (stdout only; nothing is written)

optional.when: present: the output is cross-checked with ffmpeg-skill/probe (ffmpeg_skill.status PASSED / FAILED); absent: ffmpeg_skill.status UNCHECKED

tools.description: Render a HyperFrames scene directory to video: headless Chrome captures every frame, ffmpeg encodes them; the result is probed and compared with the scene's declared size, duration and fps, and cross-checked with ffmpeg-skill's probe when an ffmpeg-skill checkout is present.
tools.dry_run: reads index.html, checks the root's declared size/duration/fps and the output path, and reports the hyperframes command it would run and the expected frame count; launches neither Chrome nor ffmpeg and writes nothing

dryRun.description: validate and plan without launching Chrome or ffmpeg or writing files

ffmpegSkill.description: ffmpeg-skill checkout to cross-check the output with (default: HYPERFRAMES_SKILL_FFMPEG_SKILL_DIR, VIDEO_AGENT_FFMPEG_SKILL_DIR, ~/.claude/skills/ffmpeg-skill, ./vendor/ffmpeg-skill, ../ffmpeg-skill next to this checkout; none found: ffmpeg_skill.status UNCHECKED)

fps.description: frame rate, integer 1-240 (default: the root's data-fps, else 30)

json.description: print one JSON result document on stdout

output.description: video file to write; its extension must match --codec

quality.description: CRF, codec-neutral scale (lower is better): h264 0-51, vp9 0-63; not for prores. Default: HyperFrames' own default (CRF 16)

timeout.description: kill the render (Chrome and ffmpeg included) after this long; 0 disables

inputs: a scene directory with index.html (from `scene`, or any HyperFrames composition whose root declares data-width, data-height and data-duration)
tools.name: render
tools.output_schema: {status, output, expected: {width, height, duration, fps, frames, codec, fps_source}, probe, hyperframes: {version, chromium: {path, source}}, verified, verification[], ffmpeg_skill: {status: PASSED|FAILED|UNCHECKED, reason?, tool, skill: {dir, source, version, version_source}|null, measured?: {duration, width, height, fps, codec, pix_fmt, alpha, frames}, checks?: [{check, ok, expected, actual}], tried?}, commands[] (hyperframes, then every chrome/ffmpeg/ffprobe process it started, then this skill's ffprobe, then ffmpeg-skill/probe when present)}
outputs: a video file (.mp4 h264, .webm vp9 or .mov prores)

tools.description: Turn a structured scene request (JSON: size, duration, fps, ordered text/image/video layers with in/out times) into a HyperFrames scene directory (index.html + copied assets).
tools.dry_run: validates the request and every asset path and reports the files it would write; writes nothing and does not run hyperframes lint

dryRun.description: validate and plan without launching Chrome or ffmpeg or writing files

json.description: print one JSON result document on stdout

output.description: scene directory to write (created; must be empty or absent)

overwrite.description: replace index.html and assets/ in a directory an earlier `scene` run wrote

inputs: the local image/video files it names
tools.name: scene
tools.output_schema: {status, output (scene dir), html, assets[], expected: {width, height, duration, fps, frames}, lint: {errors, warnings, findings[]}, verified, verification[], commands}
outputs: a scene directory: index.html and assets/

tools.description: Fill one of the skill's scene templates (lower-third, title-card, session-slate, break) with caller-given values and write the resulting scene request JSON for `scene`. --list shows every template and the values it takes.
tools.dry_run: resolves and validates the values and the filled request and reports it; writes nothing

dryRun.description: validate and plan without launching Chrome or ffmpeg or writing files

font.description: font file (.otf/.ttf/.woff2) shipped with the scene and used first for all text, e.g. a Japanese font for Japanese glyph forms

json.description: print one JSON result document on stdout

list.description: list the templates and the values each takes

inputs: values: a JSON file (--values) and/or key=value pairs (--set)
tools.name: template
tools.output_schema: {status, output, template, values (resolved, defaults included), omitted (optional values not given; their layers are left out), request, expected: {width, height, duration, fps, frames}, verified, verification[]} | --list: {status, templates: [{name, description, values}]}
